summary: Former apartheid police dog handler Louis van Schoor worked as a security guard in East London, South Africa, where he shot over a hundred mostly Black people, killing at least 39, in the late 1980s with police protection.

evidence.note: born in 1951, possibly in East London
drops out at sixteen to join the police, soon a dog-unit handler
long background on Dutch and British colonisation and the roots of apartheid
Section 49 lets police and security guards kill fleeing suspects
stepsons say he beat their mother; wife-beating and affairs
bulk of the killings from about 1986 to 1989
sub judice rule and editors block the Daily Dispatch reporting
daughter Sabrina has her mother murdered; trial in 2002
dies in July 2024, weeks before release

notes: Conviction year (1992) is from general knowledge; the transcript gives the 1991 arrest and about twelve years served. main_span starts at the c.1986 peak of the spree; approximate. Colonial and apartheid history is a long background segment, kept only as a secondary theme and excluded from covered_span. Police-dog maulings and dog necklacing get a few minutes but not enough for animal-cruelty.
